commit.description: Interactive commit with Conventional Commits format
commit.template: Run `git add .` to stage all changes, then run `git diff --staged --stat` and `git diff --staged` to understand what changed. Based on the diff, generate an appropriate Conventional Commits message in the format `type(scope): description` (omit scope if not clearly applicable). Use types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, revert. Present the proposed commit message to the user and ask for confirmation. If confirmed, run `git commit -m "<message>"` and let Husky hooks run. If the user wants changes, adjust and confirm again before committing.

quick-commit.description: Quick commit with just type and message (no scope)
quick-commit.template: Run `git add .` to stage all changes, then run `git diff --staged --stat` and `git diff --staged` to understand what changed. Based on the diff, generate a short Conventional Commits message without a scope in the format `type: description`. Use types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, revert. Present the proposed commit message to the user and ask for confirmation. If confirmed, run `git commit -m "<message>"` and let Husky hooks run. If the user wants changes, adjust and confirm again before committing.

stitch-sync.description: Sync component with Google Stitch design
stitch-sync.template: Use the google_stitch_fetch_component tool to fetch the latest design for the specified component. Compare with the current implementation and propose updates to match the Stitch design while preserving business logic and tests.

stitch-new.description: Create new component from Stitch design
stitch-new.template: Use google_stitch_generate_react_component to create a new React component from the specified Stitch design. Follow AGENTS.md structure guidelines and place in the appropriate directory (shared vs feature-specific).

stitch-tokens.template: Use google_stitch_fetch_design_tokens to get the latest design system tokens and update the project's design token files in src/styles/ to match.
